messages:
mina: heads up — saw nondeterministic eval outputs on the quantized-7b bring-up tonight. same model + same seed but metrics move ~3-5% between runs.

leo: which metric and which harness? rouge-l / exact match or something else?

mina: rouge-l (longform chat benchmark) and a small rerank test. harness: eval-runner v0.45 pinned. seed passed in via --seed.

leo: can you paste the exact CLI you ran?

mina: sure — run locally and on CI:```./eval-runner --suite longform --model redwood/quant-7b:v2 --seed 12345 --sampling-mode sampled --top_p 0.92 --temperature 0.7 --workers 4```

mina: reproducer: run twice in a row on same machine, sometimes identical; sometimes tokenization / punctuation differs at end-of-sample. weird.

arjun: are you resuming runs or doing warm start across workers? I recall a recent change where the runner toggles an experimental "sampling_phase" to switch to temperature annealing during kernel warmup.

mina: yep that's the new thing. I turned it on because latency improved, but I didn't think it would change outputs for same seed.

leo: that toggle is in runtime config:```sampling_phase: { mode: 'auto', batch_cycles: 8 }``` when mode=='auto' it uses top_p sampling for first N tokens then temperature annealing for following tokens in same request.

mina: that would explain differences across runs where requests align to different cycle boundaries. but why with same seed? seed should control RNG stream.

sophia: likely because RNG is consumed differently depending on whether sampler uses top_p or temperature paths — branching changes number of draws (e.g., top_p does reservoir-like draws vs temp uses softmax sampling), so RNG consumption count diverges even if same seed.

arjun: ^ exactly. We have two RNG flavors: legacy mt19937 per-worker and a newer counter-based Philox used in quant kernels. The handoff between them isn't deterministic if the sampler path changes mid-request.

mina: so phase switching + mixed RNG implementations + worker warmstart -> nondet. Great.

leo: quick mitigation: force sampling_phase: 'fixed' or disable auto anneal in harness to get deterministic runs. Also consider making RNG be a single counter-based stream per-request (derive stream = H(job_id, request_idx) and advance deterministically).

mina: disabling auto made results stable on my machine. CI nightly still flapped though earlier.

ci-bot: nightly/evals/quant-7b: build 2026-03-19T03:12: passed metrics but showed rouge-l variance +4.1% vs previous run. logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/quant-7b/2189

leo: can you dump per-request RNG consumption telemetry? we have sampler.op_count and rng.calls per-worker telemetry but it's pretty coarse.

arjun: plan: 1) add per-request RNG counter and deterministic seed derivation (job_id + request_idx + worker_id) 2) remove mixed RNG handoffs — use philox only for sampling kernels 3) add CI flag to run harness with sampling_phase: 'fixed' for stability tests 4) document sampling semantics in eval harness README.

mina: will open a PR for (1) and (3). linking prototype: https://git.internal/pulls/4521 (WIP).

leo: assign to arjun for (2) kernel change, needs runtime perf benchmark before merge.

sophia: I'll add a CI job that runs the nightly suite 3x and fails if variance > 2% to catch this.

mina: thanks — can we also add quick repro script that toggles sampling_phase so devs can reproduce locally?

arjun: yes will add a `scripts/repro_sampling_phase.sh` in the PR. includes commands and short log examples.

mina: cool. for now I've pinned sampling_phase='fixed' in our bring-up branch and reran — metrics stable. leaving ticket open until we unify RNG paths. :thumbsup:

leo: great triage. followups: PRs 4521, 4523, CI job nightlies/variance-check.

ci-bot: note: adding deterministic-per-request-stream will change existing archived eval hashes — label any data-change PRs with `data-migration`.
